grh_1fb3ca396d56627f3d01.title: Boy Loves Girl
paragraphs: Teenagers Hazel Miller and Bill are secretly in love and plan to marry when Hazel is eighteen, but their parents regard the relationship as childish and would separate them if they knew. Dr. Christian is aware of the romance and urges the adults to remember their own youth rather than treat the pair with contempt. After a disgruntled former employee exposes the secret, the parents react exactly as Hazel and Bill feared. The two run away to a mountain shack and, convinced they will be forced apart forever, begin talking about dying together like Romeo and Juliet. Hazel impulsively takes a pistol and shoots herself before Bill can stop her. Christian reaches the shack in time and finds that the bullet has only torn her side and the wound is not fatal. The near tragedy finally forces both families to take the young couple seriously. Their parents consent to an engagement, while marriage is postponed until Hazel and Bill are older and ready.

grh_1f41c2a68e5332f513c4.title: No Minor Vices
paragraphs: Pediatrician Perry Ashwell casually dismisses artist Octavio Quaglini's work as junk, inspiring the flamboyant painter to teach the smug doctor a lesson in emotion. Octavio insinuates himself into Perry's home and marriage, deliberately stirring jealousy by charming Perry's wife April and making Perry believe his secure domestic life may not be so secure after all. grh_1fe18157f4af2b990312.title: Music for Millions
paragraphs: Young Mike comes to New York to live with her older sister Barbara, a bassist in a women's symphony orchestra who is pregnant while her husband Joe serves overseas. When a telegram reports Joe missing and presumed dead, Barbara's friends hide the news until after the baby is born, even arranging a forged letter that appears to come from Joe so she will keep hoping. The deception nearly collapses when Barbara realizes something is wrong, but after the birth a genuine letter arrives: Joe survived months stranded after parachuting from a plane and is alive. With both Joe and the newborn safe, the orchestra changes its program to the Hallelujah Chorus in celebration.

grh_1fc684d7aad8a892f3a2.title: Mexican Hat Trick
paragraphs: A dying pickpocket's confession reveals that Vicente Coelio was wrongly accused of murder seventeen years earlier and that affidavits proving his innocence were hidden somewhere in León. Harry offers to recover the evidence for Coelio's family and travels there with Coelio's daughter Alicia, hoping to collect a large fee. He discovers that the ragged beggar shadowing them is actually Vicente, still alive and searching for the same papers. The strange change in a church bell's tone leads Harry to the affidavits hidden around its clapper. Alicia fights the beggar without realizing he is her father, and Harry later keeps Vicente's identity secret, returns the proof that clears him, and leaves León before his feelings for Alicia can keep him there.
